name: WordPress
description: WordPress project type with WP-CLI integration
author: Extra Chill

tools.remediation: Install PHP and ensure php is on PATH
Install Composer and ensure composer is on PATH
Install Node.js and ensure node is on PATH
Install npm and ensure npm is on PATH

discovery.display_name_command: cd {{basePath}} && wp option get blogname --skip-themes --skip-plugins 2>/dev/null || basename {{basePath}}

post:deploy: DEPLOY_OWNER=$(stat -c '%U:%G' {{install_dir}} 2>/dev/null || stat -f '%Su:%Sg' {{install_dir}} 2>/dev/null) && case "$DEPLOY_OWNER" in root:root) echo 'WARNING: {{install_dir}} is owned by root:root. PHP-FPM (www-data) may not be able to read plugin files.' && echo '  Fix: homeboy component set {{component_id}} remote_owner www-data:www-data' ;; esac || true

dead_guard_context_comment_patterns: (?i)pure-php smoke tests run without wordpress loaded

requested_detectors.description: SQL LIKE exact-match against JSON blob `{column}` at line {line} for key `{field}`
requested_detectors.suggestion: Avoid semantic matching inside `{column}` with LIKE. Decode candidate rows or promote `{field}` to a first-class indexed column before exact matching.

requested_detectors.label: {class}::{const}
requested_detectors.description: Raw slug literal `{value}` at line {line} duplicates constant {label}
requested_detectors.suggestion: Use {label} instead of repeating the literal slug so the constant remains the source of truth.

requested_detectors.description: Option scope drift at line {line}: docs mention network/site-option storage but implementation calls `{call}`
requested_detectors.suggestion: Use the matching site-option call or update the storage contract so multisite behaviour is explicit.

help.project_id_help: Project ID (use 'homeboy project list'). For multisite: project:subtarget
help.args_help: WP-CLI command and arguments (space-separated, not quoted)
examples: homeboy wp my-site option get blogname

declarations.description: npm dependency tree installed by this extension's bootstrap. Reconstructable from the committed package-lock.json. Resolved only beside a manifest and lockfile pair, so `npm ci` is guaranteed to restore it. A one-day floor keeps a tree that was just installed for in-flight work.

Composer dependency tree installed by this extension's bootstrap. Reconstructable from the committed composer.lock. Vendor trees that ship inside a packaged release are produced into the packaging directory, not here.

Generated JavaScript bundle output. Regenerated by the package build script, so it carries no retention cost beyond the rebuild. Resolved only beside a package manifest, which is what makes the rebuild available.
PHPUnit result cache written by this extension's test runner. Regenerated by the next run; losing it costs only test-ordering optimization.
Packaging directory. Holds both built JS assets and the deployable {component_id}.zip this extension's artifact_pattern points at, so it is inventoried for review and never reclaimed.

wp-codebox-validation.label: WP Codebox validation profile
wp-codebox-validation.summary: Run safe local build/PHPUnit smoke coverage first, then route WP Codebox benchmark work through Homeboy Lab/runner offload with durable run artifacts.
wp-codebox-validation.artifact_contract: Use Homeboy run artifacts from the build/test invocation plus the offloaded bench run artifact bundle; do not cite machine-local paths in PR evidence.

limitations: Runs the local WP Codebox-backed WordPress test runner; CI checkout/setup details such as a freshly built external wp-codebox checkout are not reproduced by the profile itself.
Runs only safe local build/package validation. It must not run benchmark workloads or Cargo/Rust validation on the Studio controller.
Runs local WP Codebox bench recipes for the current component; provider matrices, hosted runner hardware, and remote artifacts are not reproduced.
Benchmark validation is remote-only. Set /bench/local_execution to denied and pass a connected Lab/runner id so fallback cannot execute benchmarks on the controller.

settings.label: Standalone PHP test paths
settings.description: Component-relative PHP paths or shell-glob patterns that identify executable standalone PHP tests in changed-file scopes. Matching files run through the bounded host-PHP runner; PHPUnit and *-smoke.php conventions remain available without this declaration.

settings.label: Validation Dependencies
settings.description: Local component IDs or paths to load during PHPStan, autoload validation, PHPUnit, and bench. Accepts an array of component IDs, paths, or bench-scoped objects shaped like {dependency,path|slug,scenarios,profiles,profile_env}. Scoped objects let selected bench scenarios/profiles opt into expensive gateway dependencies without blocking unrelated profiles.

settings.label: WP-CLI User
settings.description: WordPress user for WP-CLI commands (email, login, or ID). When configured, automatically appended as --user flag.

settings.label: wp-config additions
settings.description: Map of CONSTANT_NAME => value appended to the WP Codebox wp-tests-config.php as additional define() statements. Lets a component declare wp-config-level constants (mode flags, debug toggles, custom paths) without shipping a custom drop-in. Values preserve PHP type via var_export() — booleans, integers, and nulls round-trip cleanly. Reserved canonical names (DB_NAME, ABSPATH, etc.) cannot be overridden.

settings.label: Build nested package.json directories
settings.description: Whether the WordPress package builder should recursively run build scripts in nested package.json directories after the root frontend build. Disable for components whose root build already produces all required nested frontend assets. Can be overridden with HOMEBOY_BUILD_NESTED_PACKAGES=0.

settings.label: Bench env passthrough
settings.description: Map of NAME => value forwarded into the WordPress runtime as environment variables. Workloads (bench) and test fixtures (test runner) read them via getenv() / $_ENV. Required because host shell env doesn't cross the sandbox boundary; without this seam, getenv('MY_KNOB') returns false regardless of what the parent shell set. Values are coerced to strings (via json_encode for non-scalars) per PHP env-var convention. Component declares static defaults; matrix drivers can synthesize HOMEBOY_SETTINGS_JSON inline to override per-cell.

settings.label: WP Codebox core module
settings.description: Host-side ESM module path or package specifier that exports WP Codebox recipe builders. Used by the bench recipe builder before sandbox launch; distinct from bench_env, which is forwarded into the WordPress runtime.

settings.label: No PHPUnit tests discovered
settings.description: How the WP Codebox PHPUnit backend treats successful WordPress install/activation when discovery finds zero PHPUnit files. Use 'skipped' for components that intentionally test through smoke scripts, or 'failed' when the component expects PHPUnit coverage. Components with phpunit.xml(.dist) still fail on zero discovery.

settings.label: npm test fallback script
settings.description: package.json script to run after WP Codebox plugin install/activation succeeds but PHPUnit discovery finds no PHPUnit files. Composer scripts.test remains the first fallback when present.

settings.label: WordPress runtime blueprint
settings.description: Backend-neutral WordPress runtime blueprint merged into the selected runtime adapter recipe. Empty object means stock WordPress. Runtime adapters normalize this canonical setting to backend-specific fields.

settings.label: WP Codebox extra plugins
settings.description: Additional WP Codebox extra plugin entries for bench recipes. Use for runtime prerequisites that must be installed or activated but should not be treated as Homeboy validation dependencies.

settings.label: WP Codebox extra themes
settings.description: Immutable local theme checkouts for the wordpress-multisite-e2e rig. Each entry is {source,slug,activate?,metadata?}; the rig validates the theme and maps it to a readonly WP Codebox mount. At most one theme may be active.

settings.label: WP Codebox dependency overlays
settings.description: Existing WP Codebox dependency overlay entries forwarded by the wordpress-multisite-e2e rig for immutable Composer package replacement.

settings.label: WordPress multisite synthetic fixture
settings.description: Run the wordpress-multisite-e2e rig's built-in alpha/beta self-test. Set false when consumer prepare/scenario/post steps own the complete network topology and journey.

settings.label: WordPress runtime workloads
settings.description: Backend-neutral WordPress workload declarations passed to the selected runtime adapter after dependency mounts and component load. Each workload declares an id, optional label, run steps ({type: 'php', code|file}, {type: 'ability', ability|name, input}, or {type: 'wp-cli', command}), and optional metrics/artifacts/metadata.

settings.label: WordPress runtime workload plugin slug
settings.description: Mounted plugin slug that owns wordpress-multisite-e2e workloads. Defaults to the synthetic fixture only while that fixture is enabled; consumer-owned topology workloads must name a declared wp_codebox_extra_plugins entry.

settings.label: WordPress runtime prepare steps
settings.description: Backend-neutral recipe steps to run before the measured WordPress runtime bench step. Each step is a runtime command object with command, args, and optional allowFailure/advisory flags. Use for generic pre-bench runtime evidence or setup that belongs outside measured workloads.

settings.label: WordPress runtime post steps
settings.description: Backend-neutral recipe steps to run after the measured WordPress runtime bench step in the same disposable runtime. Use for generic post-bench browser probes, browser actions, or reviewer-facing evidence capture after workloads mutate WordPress state.

settings.label: WP Codebox bench bootstrap files
settings.description: Component-relative bootstrap file fallbacks for WP Codebox bench workloads. The runner resolves the list against the mounted component and passes the first existing file to wordpress.bench so it loads before workloads execute.

settings.label: WP Codebox PHPUnit bootstrap mode
settings.description: How the WP Codebox PHPUnit backend prepares WordPress tests. Use 'managed' for the Homeboy-managed WordPress test bootstrap, 'project' for the component's native PHPUnit bootstrap, or 'auto' to use project mode when phpunit.xml(.dist) declares a bootstrap attribute.

settings.label: WP Codebox PHPUnit multisite
settings.description: Explicitly enable multisite for plugin PHPUnit, including plugins that are not network-only. False forces single-site; HOMEBOY_WORDPRESS_MULTISITE remains the higher-precedence runtime override.

settings.label: WP Codebox database service provider
settings.description: Optional WP Codebox MySQL-compatible service selection. Native ephemeral mode is {provider:'native',engine:'mariadb'} and accepts no connection, administration, path, process, secret_env, or network-boundary fields. External host-managed mode remains {provider:'external',engine?,allowed_hosts,secret_env:{host,port?,username,password}}; engine may be mysql or mariadb, allowed_hosts declares its external-service boundary, and secret_env maps administrative fields to host environment variable names. Omit this setting to preserve WP Codebox's default Docker provider and engine; provider:'docker' is not accepted here.

settings.label: WP Codebox PHPUnit project bootstrap
settings.description: Optional component-relative PHPUnit bootstrap path for wp_codebox_phpunit_bootstrap_mode=project. When empty, the runner reads the bootstrap attribute from phpunit.xml or phpunit.xml.dist.

settings.label: WP Codebox PHPUnit test root
settings.description: Optional sandbox path containing PHPUnit test files for wordpress.phpunit discovery. Leave empty for the mounted component tests directory. Use with wp_codebox_phpunit_mounts when the suite lives outside the component mount.

settings.label: WP Codebox PHPUnit config
settings.description: Optional sandbox path to phpunit.xml or phpunit.xml.dist for wordpress.phpunit discovery. Leave empty for the mounted component phpunit.xml.dist.

settings.label: WP Codebox PHPUnit cwd
settings.description: Optional sandbox working directory for the wordpress.phpunit process. Leave empty for the mounted component directory.

settings.label: WP Codebox PHPUnit preload files
settings.description: Absolute WP Codebox sandbox PHP files to require during managed wordpress.phpunit bootstrap. Use for runtime files that are mounted into the sandbox but are not component-root relative.

settings.label: WP Codebox PHPUnit mounts
settings.description: Additional host-to-sandbox mounts for wordpress.phpunit. Each entry is {source,target,mode?}; source must be an absolute existing host path and target an absolute sandbox path. Defaults to readonly mode.

settings.label: WP Codebox bench bootstrap steps
settings.description: Generic WP Codebox recipe steps to run during pluginRuntime.setup after dependency activation and before measured bench workloads. Use this for dependency setup that must be prepared outside workload timing.

settings.label: WP Codebox bench mounts
settings.description: Additional host-to-sandbox mounts for wordpress.bench. Each entry is {source,target,mode?}; source and target must be absolute paths. Use pre-bootstrap WordPress targets such as /wordpress/wp-content/db.php for component-owned runtime files.

settings.label: WP Codebox prepare steps
settings.description: Explicit host-side commands to run before WP Codebox mounts and loads the plugin for wordpress.bench or wordpress.phpunit. Each step is an object with command, optional string args, and optional component-relative cwd. Use this for bounded source-checkout generation such as WooCommerce feature config files; no package scripts run implicitly.

settings.label: WP Codebox source root
settings.description: Optional absolute source checkout root for WP Codebox-backed bench materialization. Use with wp_codebox_source_subpath when the selected Homeboy component path is a nested plugin but host-side prepare steps and Composer path repositories need the surrounding monorepo. Lab offload remaps path-valued --setting entries to the synced runner path before execution.

settings.label: WP Codebox source subpath
settings.description: Component-relative path under wp_codebox_source_root used as the plugin source for WP Codebox bench prep, workload discovery, file mounts, and plugin loading. Leave empty only when HOMEBOY_COMPONENT_PATH is already under wp_codebox_source_root and the runner can derive the relative path.

settings.label: WP Codebox binary
settings.description: Optional WP Codebox CLI binary path for WP Codebox-backed WordPress runtime execution. Use this to pin bench runs to a runner-local WP Codebox build with required runtime primitives. Leave empty to use HOMEBOY_WP_CODEBOX_BIN or the extension default.

settings.label: WP Codebox scenario manifests
settings.description: Scenario manifest files or inline objects compiled into wordpress.bench workloads in the generated WP Codebox recipe. Prompt, blueprint, grader, verifier hooks, rules, tags, limits, policy metadata, and metadata are preserved in BenchResults metadata.

settings.label: Bench browser target handoff
settings.description: Optional browser bench target descriptor. Set {"enabled": true} to write HOMEBOY_BENCH_SHARED_STATE/browser-target.json. Include baseUrl/adminUrl for an already-running site; otherwise the file is metadata-only because the WP Codebox bench command exits after workloads complete. Login supports method plus username/password or password_env; raw target files are handoff artifacts and must not be published in reports.

settings.label: WordPress runtime version
settings.description: Optional WordPress core version passed to WordPress test and bench runtime providers. Leave empty for the runner default. Use this when a component needs classes or behavior from a newer WordPress core build.

settings.label: WordPress multisite runtime PHP version
settings.description: Optional PHP major.minor version projected to WP Codebox runtime.phpVersion by the wordpress-multisite-e2e rig. This setting is rig-scoped; the canonical WP Codebox bench builder does not currently expose PHP selection.

settings.label: WP Codebox PHP memory limit
settings.description: Optional PHP memory_limit for WP Codebox-backed wordpress.bench runs, expressed as a PHP shorthand size such as 512M or 1G. High-cardinality bench rigs can raise this per scenario or matrix cell.

settings.label: WordPress package artifacts
settings.description: Component-relative glob patterns for intentional package ZIP artifacts that should be included in the production build even though arbitrary *.zip files are excluded by default. Supports recursive ** matching at any depth. Each declared pattern must match at least one regular file; absolute and traversal paths are rejected.

settings.label: WordPress package excludes
settings.description: Additional rsync exclude patterns applied with .buildignore/default excludes before Homeboy mandatory safety exclusions. Strings are required. Component-root rsync patterns such as /playground-runtime/ are supported; traversal and filesystem-absolute paths are rejected.

settings.label: WordPress package profile
settings.description: Optional component-relative JSON manifest and named profile that selects exact production package files after dependency preparation. Empty object keeps default rsync staging. Set {"manifest":"path.json","profile":"name"}. The named profile must provide selectors with type file or prefix and path, plus optional required_files. Manifest/profile names and all paths fail closed against absolute paths, traversal, malformed selectors, missing explicit files, and missing required files. Homeboy mandatory safety exclusions still apply.

settings.label: Additional WordPress release package profiles
settings.description: Additional package profiles published as extra release ZIP assets alongside the unchanged primary release ZIP. Each entry is {manifest, profile, artifact}: an existing package profile manifest/profile pair validated by the same fail-closed rules as package_profile, plus a basename-only .zip artifact name that must be unique across entries and cannot replace the primary ZIP. release.package builds the primary ZIP unchanged, then builds every additional profile through the same production dependency and profile-staging build path, verifies each ZIP contains the release version, and returns the primary ZIP followed by the additional assets in declared order. Malformed declarations, unsafe artifact names, and duplicates fail closed before any build runs.

settings.label: Local workspace dependency overrides
settings.description: Declared local (unpublished) workspace package dependencies to build from source, pack, and install into the consumer as a self-contained built tarball before the consumer build runs. Installing a built tarball (not a file: symlink) lets peer dependencies such as React dedupe to the consumer's single copy. Each entry is an object: name (required package name), path (required source path relative to the component, may reference sibling repos), and optional package_dir (monorepo subpackage to pack), build (explicit build command run in path; defaults to install + run build script), and package_manager (npm|pnpm|yarn, auto-detected by default).

settings.label: WordPress release provenance command
settings.description: Optional component command run after the release ZIP is staged and before it is published. The command writes a JSON object to HOMEBOY_WORDPRESS_RELEASE_SIDECAR_PATH. It receives the bounded package root, source version/tag/commit, ZIP path, and output path through HOMEBOY_WORDPRESS_RELEASE_PACKAGE_ROOT, HOMEBOY_WORDPRESS_RELEASE_SOURCE_VERSION, HOMEBOY_WORDPRESS_RELEASE_SOURCE_TAG, HOMEBOY_WORDPRESS_RELEASE_SOURCE_COMMIT, HOMEBOY_WORDPRESS_RELEASE_ZIP_PATH, and HOMEBOY_WORDPRESS_RELEASE_OUTPUT_PATH. A failing command or missing sidecar aborts release; publish verifies and uploads the resulting sidecar with the ZIP.

actions.label: Upload release ZIP to GitHub Release assets
Repin Composer custom-package to a released upstream
